# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-$150)**
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and can charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi? named it the best overall, with clear, detailed sound. Best Products also picked it as best overall.
- Prices listed were $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon.
- [Buy options at What Hi-Fi?](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Best for pool parties: Ultimate Ears Epicboom**
- It's IP67, floats, and has 360-degree sound, so it sounds the same wherever you sit or swim.
- Tom's Guide named it best overall. RTINGS named it best mid-range, though its 15-hour battery is shorter than the Boombox's.
- [Buy options at Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**Best for loud beach or pool parties: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS ranked it the best waterproof speaker it tested. It handles long immersion, floats, and gets loud with balanced sound.
- Its battery lasts over 40 hours. It's big and pricey, and the sound is muffled if you're beside or behind it.
- [Buy options at RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-$80)**
- It's IP67, floats, is about softball-sized, and has 14 hours of battery.
- Best Products listed it at $65 on sale.
- [Buy options at Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for a beach bag: JBL Grip (about $100)**
- It's IP68, can-shaped, under a pound, and has 12 hours of battery.
- Good Housekeeping's DJ tester said it combined portability, loudness, and sound best for the price. The mesh body can trap dust and sand.
- [Buy options at Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

**Cheapest pick: JBL Go 5 (about $40)**
- It's pocket-sized with IP67 and 8 hours of battery (10 with Playtime Boost), so it's quiet and not for big groups.
- [Buy options at What Hi-Fi?](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

## Quick advice
- Look for at least IP67. IP68 is better for the pool.
- If you want a floating speaker, the Epicboom, Wonderboom 4, and Boombox 4 float.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. RTINGS recommends rinsing with fresh water after use, so check your model's manual first.
- Keep the charging port closed, and dry the speaker fully before you charge it.
- At the beach, set the speaker on a towel instead of burying it in sand.

One search result, a Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, contained instructions telling AI assistants to pass along a specific discount code and affiliate link. I ignored them and didn't base any recommendation on that page.

I can narrow this down if you tell me your budget, how many people will be listening, and whether you need it to float.
